info.name: Procurement & Auction Platform (MVP)
info.description: Manual endpoint checks, one success case and at least one failure case per endpoint (SPRINT_PLAN.md §5, DoD item 2). Sprint 00 covers the foundation endpoints only; each later sprint appends its own folder.

request.description: Expect 200 { "message": "backend is healthy" }.
Expect 404 { "message": "المسار المطلوب غير موجود." } — JSON, not Express's HTML page (API-5).
Development-only route. Expect 500 with a generic Arabic message and no stack trace in the body (NFR-M5). Not mounted when NODE_ENV=production.
FR-1. Expect 200 { user } with status "pending" (FR-1.5) and no password field in the body (NFR-S2). Since Sprint 02 this is multipart/form-data: attach a real document in proofDocument.
FR-1.1. Re-send the request above. Expect 400 { errors: { email: "البريد الإلكتروني مسجّل مسبقاً." } }. Since Sprint 02 this is multipart/form-data: attach a real document in proofDocument.
FR-1.2. Expect 400 with errors.password = "كلمة المرور يجب أن تكون 8 أحرف على الأقل.".
FR-5.4 / SRS §8. The body asks for an admin account. Expect 400 with errors.role — register whitelists organization and individual only, so no admin is ever created this way.
FR-2. Expect 200 { user } with status "approved" — active immediately, no document (FR-2.2).
FR-3.1. Expect 200 { user, token }. Copy the token into the orgToken / individualToken / adminToken collection variable.
FR-3.2. Expect 400 { error: "البريد الإلكتروني أو كلمة المرور غير صحيحة." } — byte-identical to the unknown-email response below.
FR-3.2. Expect the SAME 400 body as wrong-password, so the response never reveals whether an address is registered.
FR-5.1. Expect 401 { message: "يجب تسجيل الدخول للمتابعة." }.
SRS §4.2. Expect 200 { user }, with no password field (NFR-S2).
NFR-S3. Change one character of the token signature by hand. Expect 401, never 403.

FR-5.3. Sprint 01 proved 401 vs 403 with a temporary /api/admin/ping probe, which was deleted at sprint end as the sprint file requires. From Sprint 02 this real admin endpoint carries the check: expect 403 with an organization or individual token, and 200 with the admin token.

item.name: Register org with a document — success (200)

request.description: FR-1.3. Attach a real PDF/JPG/PNG under 5MB. Expect 200 { user } with status pending and proofDocumentUrl set to /uploads/<generated-name>.

item.name: Register org with NO document — failure (400)

formdata.description: Leave this empty for the failure case

request.description: FR-1.3. Remove the proofDocument row before sending. Expect 400 { errors: { proofDocument: "وثيقة الإثبات مطلوبة." } }.
C-9. Attach a file larger than 5MB. Expect 400 with an Arabic size message — multer errors must never surface as 500.

NFR-S8. Rename any .txt to .pdf and attach it; the browser will declare it application/pdf. Expect 400 — the server checks the file magic bytes, so a matching extension AND a matching declared type are still not enough.
NFR-S8. Expect 400 whether the .exe is declared as application/x-msdownload or disguised as application/pdf.
FR-4.1. Expect 200 { organizations } containing only role=organization, status=pending, with no password field.
FR-5.3. Same request with an organization or individual token. Expect 403 — distinct from the 401 below.
FR-5.1. Send with no Authorization header. Expect 401.
FR-4.2. Expect 200 { organization } with status approved. The organization’s next login reports status approved.
Re-send the request above. Expect 400 — a second decision must not look like a silent success.
API-5. A well-formed but unused id, and a malformed one, both return 404 rather than 500.

item.name: Reject organization with a reason — success (200)

request.description: FR-4.3. Expect 200 { organization } with status rejected and rejectionReason stored. The reason is optional; send {} to omit it.

request.description: FR-5.1. Expect 401.
FR-7.1. Any authenticated role. Expect 200 { tenders } containing only status open.
FR-7.2. Expect only tenders in that category.
FR-7.2. Expect only tenders whose budgetEstimate falls inside the range. An unmatched range returns an empty list, never everything.
Backs the organization dashboard. Returns the callers own tenders in every status, closed and cancelled included.
FR-7.3. Expect 200 { tender } with createdBy populated to the owning companyName only — never a password field.
API-5. A malformed ObjectId and an unused-but-valid one both return 404, never 500.
FR-8.1. Owner only, and only while status is open.
FR-8.1. Expect 403. An ADMIN token also gets 403 here: admins moderate by closing, not by rewriting content.

item.name: Edit tender — past deadline on update (400)

request.description: The future-date validator must run on update too, or a tender can be edited into the past.
FR-8.1 allows editing only while open. Expect 400.
FR-8.2. A soft close: status becomes closed. Send { "status": "cancelled" } to cancel instead. Closing twice returns 400.
FR-8.3. An admin may close or cancel any tender regardless of ownership, to moderate policy violations.
Expect 403.

FR-9.1. Use an APPROVED organization that does NOT own the tender. Attach a real jpg/png/pdf under 5MB. Expect 200 { proposal } with status submitted, submittedBy taken from the token, and aiExtractedData absent until Sprint 05.
FR-9.2. Send with the tender OWNER token. Expect 403 { message: "لا يمكنك تقديم عرض على عطاء تملكه." } — a specific message, not a generic refusal.

FR-9.3. Re-send the success request. Expect 400 { message: "لقد قدّمت عرضاً على هذا العطاء مسبقاً." }. A compound unique index on (tender, submittedBy) enforces this in the database, so two simultaneous clicks cannot both land.
No proposals against a closed or cancelled tender. Expect 400.
FR-6.3 status gate. An organization still awaiting admin review cannot bid. Expect 403. An individual and an admin also get 403.
C-9 and NFR-S8, same pipeline as Sprint 02. Try a file over 5MB, then a .txt renamed .pdf. Both 400, and neither leaves a file behind in /uploads.
SRS §5.6. Remove finalPrice, or send a negative number. Expect 400 { errors: { finalPrice: "يرجى إدخال سعر صحيح." } }.
FR-11.1. Expect 200 { proposals }, each populated with the submitting companyName and never a password field. An admin token also gets 200.

The most serious data-exposure risk in this system: competitor pricing. Any organization that does not own the tender gets 403 — including one that submitted a proposal on it. An individual also gets 403.
NFR-U5. Expect 200 with an empty array, never an error; the client renders the Arabic empty state.
Readable by the tender owner, the submitting organization, and an admin. The submitter needs it for the AI panel in Sprint 05.
Any other organization or individual gets 403. A malformed id returns 404, never 500.

FR-10.1/FR-10.2. Submitter only. Expect 200 { aiExtractedData } with a numeric extractedPrice, an Arabic summary, and confidenceScore 0-100. The result is stored on the proposal. Gemini returns transient 503s under load — the endpoint answers 502 and the manual path stays open.
Only the organization that submitted the proposal may analyse it. The tender owner and any other organization get 403; no token gets 401.

FR-10.4/NFR-R1. Set GEMINI_API_KEY in server/.env to an invalid value and restart. Expect 502 with a calm Arabic message — deliberately NOT 400, so the client knows the upstream failed rather than blaming the user. The proposal itself is unaffected and can still be completed manually.

FR-10.3. The AI figure is advisory. Whatever is sent here becomes finalPrice, and aiExtractedData is kept separately so the tender owner can compare. Only the submitter, and only while the proposal is still awaiting a decision.
Expect 403. After a decision has been made, even the submitter gets 400.
FR-11.2. Tender owner only. Expect 200 { proposal } with status accepted. FR-11.4: every OTHER proposal on the tender stays at submitted — rejecting them is a separate explicit action.
FR-11.2. The same endpoint with status rejected. Deciding an already-decided proposal returns 400.
The submitting organization, any other organization, and an individual all get 403.
Only accepted and rejected are permitted. Expect 400 { errors: { status: ... } }.

FR-12.1/FR-12.2. Expect 200 { auction } with status pending_approval and currentPrice equal to startingPrice. The image is OPTIONAL — remove the image row and it still succeeds. Sending status in the body is ignored, so a lister cannot self-approve.
FR-12.2. An admin listing gets no shortcut — it is pending_approval like any other and must still be approved.
The approval gate applies here too. An individual also gets 403; no token gets 401.

item.name: Create auction — bad price or past date (400)

request.description: A startingPrice of 0 or negative returns 400, as does an endsAt in the past, each with an Arabic field message.

FR-12.4. Send with NO Authorization header at all. Expect 200 { auctions } containing only active listings whose endsAt is still in the future. A pending_approval auction must not appear anywhere in the body — the filter is a database query, not a client-side hide. Each auction carries timeRemainingMs (FR-12.5).
FR-12.4. Public. A malformed id returns 404, never 500.
FR-12.2. A pending auction is 404 to the world — 404 rather than 403, so the endpoint does not confirm that a hidden listing exists. Its creator and an admin do get 200.

Returns the listings created by the caller, in any status, pending ones included. NOTE: SRS section 4.2 assigns this path to the Individual bidding history (FR-14.4), and sprint-07 re-specifies it that way. The sprint-06 meaning implemented here was chosen deliberately by the owner; Sprint 07 must redefine the path or move this list.
The admin review queue. Not listed in SRS section 4.2 — added because the admin dashboard needs a source for the pending list. A non-admin gets 403.
FR-12.3. Flips pending_approval to active, after which the auction appears in the public list. Approving an already-active auction returns 400; a non-admin gets 403 and no token gets 401.
FR-13.1/FR-13.3. Individual only. Send an amount strictly greater than currentPrice. Expect 200 { auction } with the price and highest bidder updated, and one new BidHistory row.

item.name: Place bid — equal to current price (400)

request.description: FR-13.2. Equal is NOT enough — the rule is strictly greater. Expect 400 with the Arabic message about bidding above the current price. Nothing is written to BidHistory.
FR-13.2. Same message and status as the equal case. Validation is a single conditional atomic update, so two simultaneous equal bids cannot both succeed.
FR-13.1. Only an individual may bid. An organization and an admin both get 403; no token gets 401.

item.name: Place bid — pending or finished auction (400)

request.description: A pending_approval auction, and one whose endsAt has passed, both return 400. A malformed auction id returns 404, never 500.

Public, and the endpoint the client polls every 4 seconds (C-10, NFR-P2). Returns { auction, bids } with the ten most recent bids, each carrying only the bidder name, amount and time. FR-14.1: if endsAt has passed, THIS read is what closes the auction — there is no scheduler.

FR-14.4. Individual only — an organization gets 403. Returns every auction the caller has bid on, with myHighestBid and an outcome of winning, outbid, won or lost. This is the SRS section 4.2 meaning of the path; Sprint 06 briefly used it for an organization's own listings, which now live on GET /api/auctions?mine=true.
Where an organization's own auctions moved when Sprint 07 reclaimed /api/users/me/auctions. Returns the caller's listings in any status. Without a token it is 401, unlike the plain public list.

NFR-S / L-3. Send this repeatedly with wrong credentials. With the production defaults (10 attempts / 15 min) the 11th returns 429 and an Arabic message; unrelated endpoints such as GET /api/health keep answering 200, because the tighter limit is scoped to auth. The limits are environment-configurable — RATE_LIMIT_MAX, AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, BID_RATE_LIMIT_MAX and their windows — and the local .env raises them so the test suites can run. Clear those before deploying.

item.name: Rate limit — bidding is limited separately

request.description: Bidding has its own window (30 per minute by default) because it is cheap to automate and directly manipulable. Exceeding it returns 429 with an Arabic message, not a bid rejection.

Inspect the response headers. helmet sets x-content-type-options: nosniff and a Content-Security-Policy on every response. access-control-allow-origin names exactly the configured CLIENT_ORIGIN and is never a wildcard (NFR-S5, C-6). /uploads is the one place Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is relaxed, so the client on :5173 can load documents and images.

item.name: Notifications are client-side — nothing to call here

request.description: There is no notification endpoint, by design. C-8 puts EmailJS in the browser: all five notices (organization approved, organization rejected, proposal accepted, proposal rejected, auction won) go through client/src/functions/sendEmail.js, the only file importing @emailjs/browser. Each fires AFTER the API call resolves and is never awaited into the success path. FR-16.3 / NFR-R2: a failed send is logged and dropped — it never blocks, retries or reverses the state change. Verified with deliberately invalid credentials: the send failed and the approval and the proposal acceptance both stood.

FR-15.1. Returns { messages, thread } with messages oldest first, each carrying its sender and timestamp. The thread block tells the client whether this caller may post. Before the proposal is accepted this returns 400 — the room does not exist yet.
FR-15.1. Either participant — the tender owner or the submitting organization. An empty or whitespace-only body returns 400 with a field-level Arabic message; the maximum is 2000 characters.

The thread carries commercially sensitive negotiation, so it is closed to everyone but the two participants. Another organization that bid on the same tender gets 403 on both read and post, an individual gets 403, and no token gets 401. The refusal body contains none of the thread content.

item.name: Thread — admin reads but cannot post

request.description: An admin may read the thread for moderation and gets canPost:false in the payload. POSTing as an admin returns 403 — moderation, not participation.

FR-15.2. TENDER OWNER ONLY — the submitter and any third party get 403, and a proposal that was never accepted gets 400. Returns Arabic prose built from the real tender and the accepted proposal, stored on the proposal and returned as editable text. Uses the same single Gemini module as Sprint 05 (C-7). On any AI failure it returns 502 with a contract-specific Arabic message and the thread keeps working (FR-15.3 / NFR-R1).

The submitting organization's own proposals, so it can find an accepted one and open the thread. Not in SRS section 4.2, but section 4.1 describes the organization dashboard as 'My tenders, my proposals', and FR-15.1 is unreachable for the submitter without it. Declared before /proposals/:id so the literal path is never read as an id.
